easy.def: A word for a boy or a man.
examples: He is my brother.
He plays the drums.
My dad said he is hungry.

more.def: A word used for a boy, a man, or a male animal that has already been talked about.
examples: My uncle lives far away, but he visits every summer.
The rooster crowed because he woke up early.

easy.def: The top part of your body with your face.
examples: I wear a hat on my head.
She nodded her head.
The dog shook its head.

more.def: The top part of the body, which holds the brain, eyes, ears, nose, and mouth.
examples: He put a helmet on his head before riding his bike.
The giraffe lifted its head high to reach the leaves.

easy.def: A pain in your head.

more.def: A pain in the head.
examples: I had a headache after being in the sun.

easy.def: A band worn around the head.

The headband kept her hair out of her eyes.

easy.def: The board at the head of a bed.

more.def: A board or panel at the top end of a bed, behind the pillows.

easy.def: A fancy hat for special days.

more.def: A fancy covering or decoration worn on the head, often for special events.

more.def: In soccer, a shot or pass made by hitting the ball with the head.

The goalie caught the header.

easy.def: With your head going first.

more.def: With the head going in front of the body.

She slid headfirst into the base.

easy.def: Hats and helmets.

more.def: Anything worn on the head, such as a hat or helmet.

easy.def: A light worn on the head.

more.def: A lamp worn on the head to light your way; or a headlight on a car.

more.def: A high piece of land that sticks out into the sea.

more.def: The main performer or the most important act in a show.

easy.def: Something worn on the head.

more.def: The process of becoming well again after being sick or hurt.

more.def: A flat landing place for helicopters.
examples: The helicopter landed on the hospital helipad.
A helipad is marked with a big H.
The helipad was on top of the building.

easy.def: A light gas that makes balloons float.
examples: The balloon has helium in it.
Helium makes a balloon go up.
Helium is a gas.

more.def: A very light gas with no color or smell that is used to make balloons float.
examples: The party balloons were filled with helium.
Helium is lighter than air, so balloons rise.
Breathing helium makes your voice sound funny, but it is not safe to do much.

easy.def: A shape that spirals around.
examples: A helix is a spiral.
The helix twists.
The spring is a helix.

more.def: A spiral shape, like a coil or a spiral staircase.
examples: A spring is shaped like a helix.
The snail's shell is a helix.
The DNA molecule has a double helix shape.

easy.def: A word you say when you meet someone.
examples: Hello, Mom!
Say hello to Grandpa.
Hello, my name is Ben.

more.def: A word used to greet someone or to start a phone call.
examples: Hello, how are you today?
She said hello to the new student with a smile.
I picked up the phone and said hello.

easy.def: The wheel that turns a ship.
examples: The captain stood at the helm.
She held the helm.
The helm turned.

more.def: The wheel or handle used to steer a boat or ship.
examples: The captain stood at the helm and steered through the storm.
She took the helm while the others rested.
The helm is at the back of the boat.

easy.def: A hard hat that protects your head.
examples: I wear a helmet on my bike.
The helmet is blue.
Put on your helmet.

more.def: A strong, hard hat that protects your head.
examples: I wear a helmet when I ride my bike.
The football player buckled his helmet.
Workers wear a helmet on the building site.

easy.def: The person who turns the wheel of a ship.
examples: The helmsman steered.
A helmsman holds the wheel.
The helmsman looked ahead.

more.def: The person who steers a ship or boat.
examples: The helmsman steered the ship through the storm.
A helmsman must watch the waves and wind.
The captain asked the helmsman to turn left.

easy.def: To do something for someone to make it easier.
examples: I help my mom.
She helped him up.
Can you help me?

more.def: To make something easier or better for someone by doing part of the work.
examples: The children helped the teacher carry the boxes of books.
Rain helps the flowers grow in spring.
Neighbors came to help after the storm.

easy.def: Something you do to make things easier for someone.
examples: Thank you for your help.
I need help.
He asked for help.

more.def: The act of giving someone support, or anything that is useful to someone.
examples: The lost hiker called for help and the rangers came quickly.
My brother's help made cleaning the garage much faster.
A map is a great help when you are traveling.

easy.def: A person who helps.
examples: She is my helper.
The helper carried the box.
Every helper got a sticker.

more.def: A person or thing that helps someone do a job.
examples: My brother is a good helper in the kitchen.
The teacher chose a helper to hand out the papers.
A friendly helper carried the groceries for us.

easy.def: Ready to help.
examples: She is a helpful girl.
The map was helpful.
He is always helpful.

more.def: Giving help, or useful.
examples: The librarian was very helpful.
The map was helpful on our hike.
He is a helpful neighbor.

easy.def: Not able to help yourself.
examples: The baby is helpless.
A helpless kitten cried.
The turtle on its back was helpless.

more.def: Not able to take care of yourself or to do anything.
examples: A newborn baby is helpless.
The kitten was helpless in the tree.
The turtle felt helpless on its back.

easy.def: A phone number to call for help.
examples: He called the helpline.
The helpline gave advice.
A helpline answers.

more.def: A telephone service that people can call to get help or advice.
examples: She called the helpline for advice.
The helpline is open all day.
A helpline can answer your questions.

easy.def: The folded edge sewn at the bottom of clothes.
examples: Mom fixed the hem.
The hem of my dress came loose.
The hem is sewn.

more.def: The folded and sewn edge at the bottom of a piece of cloth or clothing.
examples: Grandma fixed the hem on my pants.
The hem of her dress dragged on the ground.
A loose thread hung from the hem.

easy.def: To sew a folded edge on cloth.
examples: Grandma will hem the skirt.
She hemmed my pants.
I hem the cloth.

more.def: To fold over the edge of cloth and sew it.
examples: Grandma hemmed my pants so they were not too long.
She hemmed the curtains by hand.
Dad hemmed the cloth to stop it from fraying.

easy.def: One half of the Earth.
examples: We live in the Northern Hemisphere.
A hemisphere is half.
The southern hemisphere.

more.def: One half of the Earth, divided by the equator into north and south or by a line into east and west.
examples: We live in the Northern Hemisphere, where it is summer in July.
Australia is in the Southern Hemisphere, so its seasons are opposite to ours.
The brain has two hemispheres, a left one and a right one.

easy.def: The bottom edge of a dress or skirt.
examples: The hemline is long.
A hemline is the bottom edge.
Check the hemline.

more.def: The bottom edge of a skirt, dress or coat.
examples: The dress has a long hemline.
She shortened the hemline.
The hemline brushed her shoes.

easy.def: A grown-up female chicken.
examples: The hen laid an egg.
A hen sat on the nest.
The hen has chicks.

more.def: A female chicken, or the female of some other birds.
examples: The hen laid a brown egg in the straw.
A hen clucked as she led her chicks across the yard.
A mother hen keeps her eggs warm until they hatch.

easy.def: For that reason.
examples: It was raining, hence the wet floor.
He is tired, hence the yawn.
It is cold, hence our coats.

more.def: For that reason; as a result.
examples: The road was icy, hence the long delay for the school bus.
She practiced every day, hence her great improvement on the violin.
The shop is closed on Mondays, hence the empty street.

easy.def: A small building where hens sleep.
examples: The hens are in the henhouse.
The henhouse is small.
We gather eggs in the henhouse.

more.def: A small house or shed where hens are kept.
examples: We collected eggs from the henhouse.
The farmer locked the henhouse at night.
The fox prowled around the henhouse.

easy.def: A shape with seven sides.
examples: A heptagon has seven corners.
Draw a heptagon.
The heptagon is a shape.

more.def: A flat shape with seven straight sides and seven angles.
examples: A heptagon has seven sides.
She drew a heptagon on the board.
The coin was shaped like a heptagon.

easy.def: A word for a girl or a woman.
examples: I gave her a card.
Mom has her coat.
Tell her the news.

more.def: A word used for a girl, a woman, or a female animal, either as the one receiving an action or as the owner of something.
examples: We threw a party to thank her for the help.
Her bicycle has a bell and a basket.
The teacher asked her to read the poem aloud.

easy.def: A person who brings news long ago.
examples: The herald blew a horn.
A herald came with news.
The king's herald spoke.

more.def: A person in the past whose job was to bring news and make announcements for a king or queen.
examples: The herald blew a trumpet and read the king's message to the town.
A herald rode into the village with big news.
The herald stood on the castle steps and announced the feast.

easy.def: To announce that something is coming.
examples: Birds herald spring.
The bell heralded the start.
A trumpet heralded the king.

more.def: To show or announce that something is about to happen.
examples: Robins heralded the spring by singing in the trees.
A trumpet heralded the arrival of the king.
The first snow heralded the start of winter.

easy.def: A plant used to flavor food.
examples: Mint is an herb.
I grow herbs.
The herb smells nice.

more.def: A leafy plant that is used to flavor food or to make medicine.
examples: Basil is an herb used in pasta sauce.
Mom grows herbs on the windowsill.
Fresh herbs make soup taste good.

easy.def: Made from plants.
examples: Herbal tea.
An herbal drink.
I like herbal tea.

more.def: Made from herbs or plants.
examples: She drank a cup of herbal tea.
The herbal soap smelled of lavender.
Herbal medicines come from plants.

easy.def: A poison that kills weeds.
examples: Herbicide kills weeds.
The herbicide is strong.
He sprayed herbicide.

more.def: A chemical that is used to kill weeds and unwanted plants.
examples: The farmer sprayed herbicide on the weeds.
Herbicide can harm other plants too.
Keep herbicide away from pets.

easy.def: An animal that eats only plants.
examples: A cow is a herbivore.
The herbivore eats grass.
Rabbits are herbivores.

more.def: An animal that eats only plants.
examples: A cow is a herbivore that eats grass.
Herbivores have flat teeth for chewing leaves.
The giraffe is a herbivore that eats tree leaves.

easy.def: Plants with leaves used to give food a good taste.
examples: Mom grows herbs in pots.
The soup has herbs.
We picked herbs.

more.def: Plants such as mint, basil and parsley, whose leaves are used to flavor food or to make medicine.
examples: Mom grows mint, basil and other herbs in pots on the windowsill.
The soup was seasoned with fresh herbs from the garden.
Long ago, people used herbs to make tea for a sore throat.

easy.def: A group of animals that stay together.
examples: A herd of cows crossed the road.
The herd of deer ran.
The herd moved.

more.def: A large group of animals of the same kind that live or move together.
examples: The herd of bison moved slowly across the plain.
The herd of elephants drank at the river.
The deer herd moved through the forest.

easy.def: A person who looks after a herd.
examples: The herder watched the sheep.
A herder guides animals.
The herder whistled.

more.def: A person who looks after a herd of animals.
examples: The herder led the sheep up the hill.
A goat herder has a strong stick.
The herder whistled to his dog.

easy.def: A man who looks after a herd.
examples: The herdsman watched the cattle.
A herdsman guides cows.
The herdsman whistled.

more.def: A man whose job is to look after a herd of animals.
examples: The herdsman led the cattle to the hills.
A herdsman guides the cows to water.
The herdsman whistled to his dog.

easy.def: In this place.
examples: Come here, please.
I live here.
Put the box here.

more.def: In or to the place where you are, or at this point in time.
examples: Our class has been here at the museum all morning.
Please bring your chair over here, next to the window.
Spring is here, and the flowers are blooming.

easy.def: Things from the past that we keep.
examples: We share our heritage.
Our heritage is important.
She learned about her heritage.

more.def: The customs, stories and traditions that are passed down from earlier generations, or the places and buildings that are saved from the past.
examples: Our class learned about each family's heritage and the foods they eat at holidays.
The old castle is part of the country's heritage.
She is proud of her heritage and tells the family stories to her children.

easy.def: A person who lives alone away from others.
examples: The hermit lived alone.
A hermit lived in a cave.
The hermit liked quiet.

more.def: A person who chooses to live alone, away from other people.
examples: A hermit lived alone in a cabin in the woods.
The hermit grew his own food and spoke to nobody.
In the story, a wise hermit gave the travelers advice.

easy.def: A quiet place where someone lives alone.
examples: He lived in a hermitage.
The hermitage was quiet.
A hermitage is hidden.

more.def: A quiet, faraway place where a person lives alone.
examples: The old man lived in a hermitage deep in the woods.
The hermitage was a tiny stone hut.
A path led to the hermitage on the hill.

easy.def: A brave person who helps others.
examples: The firefighter is a hero.
My mom is my hero.
The hero in the story saves the town.

more.def: A person admired for being brave or for doing something great.
examples: She became a hero when she saved the child from the river.
The dog was called a hero for waking the family during the fire.
My hero is the scientist who found the cure.

easy.def: Very brave.
examples: The heroic firefighter saved the cat.
A heroic act.
She was heroic.

more.def: Showing great courage like a hero.
examples: The heroic firefighter rescued the kitten.
It was a heroic effort to climb the peak.
The dog's heroic act saved the child.

easy.def: A girl or woman who is brave or is the main character.
examples: The heroine saved the day.
A brave heroine.
The heroine of the story.

more.def: A woman or a girl who is admired for being brave or good, or the main female character in a story.
examples: The heroine of the story rescued her friends from the cave.
She was a heroine for saving the little boy from the water.
The movie's heroine was clever and kind.

easy.def: Great bravery.
examples: The firefighter showed heroism.
The girl showed heroism.
We admire her heroism.

more.def: Great courage, especially when helping others.
examples: The firefighter was praised for her heroism.
The boy's heroism saved the little dog.
The class read a story about heroism.

easy.def: A tall bird with long legs that stands in water.
examples: A heron stood in the pond.
The heron has long legs.
I saw a heron.

more.def: A tall wading bird with long legs, a long neck and a sharp beak that catches fish.
examples: A heron stood still in the shallow water.
The heron stretched out its long neck and caught a fish.
Herons build their nests in tall trees.

easy.def: A small silver fish that swims in big groups.
examples: A herring swam by.
Herring live in the sea.
We ate herring for lunch.

more.def: A small, silver sea fish that swims in huge schools and is eaten by people, whales and seabirds.
examples: Millions of herring swim together in huge, flashing schools.
Seabirds and whales feed on herring in the cold ocean.
The fisherman's net came up full of silver herring.

easy.def: A pattern of zigzag lines.
examples: The jacket is herringbone.
A herringbone pattern.
The floor has herringbone.

more.def: A pattern of zigzag lines that looks like the bones of a fish.
examples: His jacket had a herringbone pattern.
The bricks were laid in herringbone.
The scarf was woven in a herringbone design.

easy.def: Belonging to her.
examples: The red coat is hers.
This book is hers.
Is the dog hers?

more.def: Used to show that something belongs to a girl or woman.
examples: The winning ticket was hers.
This pencil is mine, and that one is hers.
The prize was hers.

easy.def: She, and not someone else.
examples: She made lunch herself.
She hurt herself.
Mia sees herself in the mirror.

more.def: Used to talk about a girl or woman who has just been named, as the one who does or gets the action.
examples: She taught herself to play the guitar.
Maria made a cake all by herself.
The little girl dressed herself.

easy.def: Slow to act because you are not sure.
examples: I was hesitant to jump.
She felt hesitant.
He gave a hesitant answer.

more.def: Slow to act or speak because you are unsure or nervous.
examples: I was hesitant to jump off the high diving board.
She gave a hesitant answer because she was not sure it was right.
The hesitant puppy stood at the edge of the water.

easy.def: In a slow way, because you are not sure.
examples: She hesitantly raised her hand.
He hesitantly stepped in.
The girl spoke hesitantly.

more.def: In a slow, unsure way, as if you are not ready to act.
examples: She hesitantly raised her hand to answer.
He hesitantly stepped onto the ice.
The boy hesitantly knocked on the door.

easy.def: To stop for a moment because you are not sure.
examples: I hesitate before I jump in the pool.
The cat hesitated at the door.
Do not hesitate to ask for help.

more.def: To pause before doing something because you feel unsure or nervous.
examples: He hesitated at the door, wondering if he should knock.
She hesitated before answering the hard question.
The deer hesitated at the edge of the road.

easy.def: Stopping for a moment because you are unsure.
examples: He answered without hesitation.
A moment of hesitation.
She jumped without hesitation.

more.def: A short pause before you do or say something, because you are not sure.
examples: He answered the question without hesitation.
After a moment of hesitation, she jumped into the pool.
There was a hesitation in his voice when he spoke.

easy.def: To chop or cut with an ax.
examples: He hewed the log.
The woodcutter hewed a tree.
They hew wood.

more.def: To cut or shape something by chopping with an ax or other tool.
examples: He hewed a log into a bench.
The woodcutter hewed down the old oak.
They hewed steps in the rock.

easy.def: A shape with six sides.
examples: A hexagon has six sides.
The tile is a hexagon.
Draw a hexagon.

more.def: A flat shape with six straight sides.
examples: A honeycomb cell is a hexagon.
Bees build their honeycomb out of tiny hexagons.
She drew a hexagon on the board.

easy.def: Having six sides.
examples: The tile is hexagonal.
A hexagonal box.
The hexagonal cell.

more.def: Having six straight sides and six angles.
examples: The box was hexagonal.
A honeycomb is made of hexagonal cells.
The room had a hexagonal floor.

easy.def: A word used to get someone's attention.
examples: Hey, wait for me!
Hey, look at that!
Hey, how are you?

more.def: A word you call out to get someone's attention or to greet them.
examples: Hey, you dropped your glove!
Hey, look at that big bird!
Hey, what a great idea!
